job.title: Production Supervisor
job.description:
Production Supervisor

Full-Time | Manufacturing / Production

$26.00 - $31.00 per hour DOE

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Production Supervisor to lead daily production activities and supervise employees on the manufacturing floor.

This position works closely with the Plant Manager to ensure production schedules are met, quality standards are maintained, employees are properly trained, and the production area operates safely and efficiently.

The ideal candidate is an experienced manufacturing leader with strong organizational and problem-solving skills and a background in Lean Six Sigma or continuous improvement.

What You'll Do

  • Supervise daily production activities and employees across assigned work cells or production lines.
  • Set up and assign orders to the appropriate production areas.
  • Monitor production schedules and ensure customer delivery dates are met.
  • Monitor jobs in progress and perform quality checks as needed.
  • Review and release work orders and ensure production documentation is complete and accurate.
  • Determine staffing and labor requirements and make recommendations regarding personnel.
  • Train and coach production employees and temporary workers on job duties, procedures, and safety.
  • Work with the Quality team to improve processes and update production procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe production environment.
  • Ensure materials are handled, stored, and disposed of properly.
  • Coordinate requests for labels, materials, and equipment as needed.
  • Identify production issues and help develop practical solutions to improve efficiency and quality.
  • Follow all company safety policies, procedures, and regulations.
  • Promote safe work practices and hold employees accountable for following safety standards.

What We're Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED required; college education preferred.
  • 5+ years of manufacturing or production experience.
  • 3+ years of experience supervising or managing employees.
  • Lean Six Sigma training and hands-on continuous improvement experience.
  • Strong knowledge of production processes and workflow.
  • Experience using computers and Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word, and Excel.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to understand and follow written and verbal instructions.
  • Ability to perform basic math and accurately count materials.
  • Strong teamwork and leadership skills.
  • Reliable attendance and punctuality.
  • Spanish/English bilingual skills are a plus, but not required.
  • Pallet jack experience and forklift certification are preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull up to 30 pounds; additional weight may be handled with assistance.
  • Ability to stand, walk, and work on a manufacturing floor for extended periods.
  • Ability to safely operate or work around production equipment and material-handling equipment.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to take a hands-on leadership role in a manufacturing environment where you can directly influence production performance, quality, employee development, safety, and continuous improvement.

Job Type: Full-Time

Department: Production

Reports To: Plant Manager

job.title: Terminal Manager
job.description:
Terminal Operations Manager

Lake Panasoffkee, FL | Full-Time

$95,000.00


About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Terminal Operations Manager to oversee the daily operations of a transportation terminal in Lake Panasoffkee, FL.

This position plays a key role in managing terminal profitability, transportation costs, fleet utilization, safety, customer service, and employee performance. The Terminal Operations Manager will lead both office and driver personnel while ensuring the terminal operates safely, efficiently, and cost-effectively.

If you have experience in transportation, logistics, fleet operations, dispatch, or terminal management and are ready to take on a leadership role, we'd like to hear from you.


What You'll Do

  • Oversee daily terminal operations, including drivers, office personnel, equipment, routing, and capacity.
  • Analyze routing, lane mix, transportation modes, and operating costs to improve efficiency and profitability.
  • Monitor available loads and capacity and work with dispatch, brokerage, and sales teams to address changing transportation needs.
  • Ensure orders are entered accurately, appointments are scheduled, equipment is assigned, and shipments are processed on time.
  • Lead, coach, and provide ongoing performance feedback to drivers and office employees.
  • Monitor operational and financial performance and communicate results and cost concerns to management.
  • Help establish freight rates and negotiate rates with outside carriers.
  • Monitor supply and demand and adjust resources to maintain appropriate capacity.
  • Support customer service objectives while balancing service levels with transportation costs.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety and ensure compliance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Assist with driver safety meetings, training, counseling, and disciplinary matters when appropriate.
  • Assist with accident response and investigations as needed.
  • Monitor vehicle and trailer maintenance, inspections, repairs, fuel usage, and overall equipment condition.
  • Coordinate preventive maintenance and repairs to keep equipment safe and available.
  • Review equipment and roadside inspection results and ensure identified issues are addressed before equipment returns to service.
  • Identify opportunities to improve fleet utilization, reduce operating costs, and increase profitability.
  • Make day-to-day decisions involving drivers, equipment, routing, carriers, rates, and customer service.


What We're Looking For

  • 2–3 years of transportation, logistics, fleet, or terminal operations experience, or equivalent education and experience.
  • Previous supervisory or management experience preferred.
  • Knowledge of transportation operations, routing, capacity planning, and cost management.
  • Strong leadership and communication skills.
  • Ability to analyze operational information and make sound business decisions.
  • Strong problem-solving and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and respond to unexpected operational issues.
  • Basic computer skills and proficiency with standard office software.
  • Strong mathematical and analytical skills.
  • Ability to read and understand transportation regulations and company procedures.
  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Reliable attendance and a commitment to workplace safety.


Key Skills

Transportation Operations | Terminal Management | Fleet Management | Logistics | Dispatch | Cost Control | Routing | Carrier Management | Safety Compliance | Employee Supervision | Customer Service | Problem Solving


Why Join Us?

  • Leadership position with significant responsibility and visibility
  • Opportunity to manage and develop a transportation team
  • Direct impact on terminal performance and profitability
  • Fast-paced, hands-on work environment
  • Opportunity for professional growth within the transportation industry


Safety-Sensitive Position

This is a safety-sensitive position. The role involves working around commercial vehicles, drivers, trailers, and transportation equipment. Employees must follow all company safety policies and applicable state and federal regulations.


Physical Requirements

This position requires the ability to sit, stand, walk, talk, and see in order to perform essential job duties. The work environment may include moderate noise and exposure to transportation and fleet operations.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

job.title: A Sales Representative

No cold calling. No prospecting for appointments. Prospects are provided.

No timeshare experience required.

  • Ongoing coaching and development

What You'll Do

As a Sales Representative, you'll meet face-to-face with prospective customers and current guests, learn about their vacation interests, and introduce them to vacation ownership opportunities.

  • Conduct scheduled vacation ownership presentations with qualified prospective customers
  • Build rapport, ask questions, and identify customer needs
  • Present ownership options, features, and benefits

  • Complete required sales paperwork and documentation

Continually develop your presentation and closing skills

Previous timeshare experience is not required. We're looking for people who are confident with customers, motivated by results, coachable, dependable, and comfortable in a performance-driven sales environment.

You do not need to currently hold a timeshare license to apply.

Compensation

This is a 1099 independent-contractor, commission-based sales opportunity with a draw against earned commissions.

  • Uncapped earning potential
  • Higher earnings are possible based on individual sales performance

Ready to Build a Career in Sales?

If you're confident with people, motivated by results, and interested in an opportunity where customers are provided and your earning potential isn't capped, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Talent Director
job.description:
Talent Director – North America

Location: 100% Remote – U.S.

Compensation: Up to $160,000 annually

Travel: Approximately 10–15%

Reports to: North America HR Vice President


Build the Talent Strategy. Develop the Leaders. Shape the Future.

Our client is seeking an accomplished Talent Director to build and lead an integrated talent strategy across its North American organization.


This is an opportunity for a highly analytical, intellectually curious HR leader who understands the business and can translate organizational needs into practical talent solutions. You’ll have broad responsibility across talent acquisition, learning and development, performance management, leadership development, succession planning, and early-career talent.

This is a highly visible role for a strategic, hands-on leader who enjoys building programs and processes, not simply maintaining them.


What You’ll Lead

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive North American talent strategy and annual roadmap.
  • Provide strategic leadership for talent acquisition, including recruiting strategy, processes, workforce planning, candidate experience, and metrics.
  • Build scalable learning and development programs for employees, managers, and leaders.
  • Design and lead a consistent performance-management and annual review process, including manager training, tools, communications, and governance.
  • Develop leadership-development programs across multiple levels of the organization.
  • Establish succession planning and talent-review processes to identify high-potential talent, assess bench strength, and strengthen the leadership pipeline.
  • Design and lead a structured internship and early-career talent program.
  • Partner with senior leaders and HR Business Partners to translate business priorities into effective talent strategies.
  • Establish meaningful talent metrics and use data to evaluate effectiveness and guide decisions.


What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate combines intellectual horsepower, business acumen, and practical execution. You can quickly understand complex challenges, develop thoughtful solutions, influence senior leaders, and personally drive initiatives from concept through implementation.


Key qualifications include:

  • 10+ years of progressive Human Resources and/or Talent Management experience
  • 5+ years of HR Business Partner experience, ideally supporting business or operational leadership
  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience in talent acquisition and recruiting
  • Strong experience with learning and development and leadership development
  • Demonstrated success designing and implementing performance-management and performance-review processes
  • Experience building succession-planning and talent-review programs
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, project-management, and communication skills
  • Ability to influence and partner effectively with senior leadership


Experience building or transforming a talent function within a geographically dispersed, multi-site, technical, industrial, engineering, or professional-services organization is highly valued. An advanced degree is a plus.


Who Will Thrive Here

You’re a builder who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. You’re intellectually curious, analytical, pragmatic, and comfortable challenging assumptions. You know how to create structure without unnecessary bureaucracy and understand how talent decisions ultimately affect business performance.

If you’ve built expertise across recruiting, development, performance, and succession—and you’re ready to bring those disciplines together into an integrated talent strategy—this is an opportunity to make a significant and lasting impact.

Compensation: Up to $160,000 annually, based on qualifications and experience.


This search is being conducted confidentially by RCI on behalf of its client. Additional information about the organization will be shared with qualified candidates during the recruitment process.

job.description:
Detention Officers

Carlsbad, NM


If you are interested in launching a law enforcement career, Eddy County is offering an amazing opportunity. It has a rich history and continues to grow and flourish with great schools, regional places of interest, the Carlsbad Caverns National Park, and other resources! Come join the law enforcement team in this exciting county!


The Perks!

  • $5K Sign-On Bonus! (2nd half paid after 1 year)
  • Earn $26.21/hr. (up to $28.23/hr. for 5+ years of exp.)
  • Great training and advancement opportunities
  • Full range of employee benefits: 
  • Paid personal leave time 
  • Paid holidays
  • Sick leave
  • Employer provided Insurance: Medical, Dental Vision, and Life
  • Employee Assistance
  • Education Assistance
  • Retirement as part of Public Employees Retirement Association (PERA) 
  • And more!


We’re Recourse Communications and we match top talent with top opportunities. As an Eddy County Detention Officer, you will ultimately maintain the immediate security, care, and control of inmates at the Eddy County Detention Center. You will supervise and monitor behavior of residents, and coordinate and cooperate with law enforcement agencies and judiciary agencies, as necessary. You will plan and perform a wide range of detention duties to ensure the proper booking, incarceration and safety of persons committed to the Detention Center, inspect facilities for cleanliness, clean and sanitize the facility, identify and report conditions or practices that may compromise overall sanitation effectiveness, maintain an inventory of sanitation supplies, maintain and inventory of all inmate supplies, stored clothing and distribution. You may transport prisoners to court and other appearances, and you must perform all duties with minimal supervision.
